label: models/fw_walllamp.mdl: a caged wall lamp with a sodium-orange glass

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl, models/ribcage.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: All ten views in sides.png show a plain cube with square outlines in every orthographic view. Nothing in it reads as a caged wall lamp. There is no wall plate or mount, no rounded or domed glass, and no cage bars breaking the outline.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size, so there is nothing to measure against. The model is 24 x 24 x 24. A wall lamp is usually shallow front to back and smaller than that, and a 24-unit cube is too deep and bulky for one. The size is not absurd, but it is clearly off for the subject.

M3.reason: None of the lamp's parts are there. There is no cage, no glass globe or lens, no wall backplate or bracket, and no bulb housing. The model is a single box with six identical faces.

M4.reason: Every face in every view is the same flat mid-grey with a faint concrete grain. The brief asks for sodium-orange glass inside a metal cage. Nothing is orange, nothing reads as glass, and nothing reads as painted or rusted metal.

M5.reason: There are no cage bars, rivets, panel lines, wear, or lit or glowing glass. The only surface detail is a uniform concrete-like noise, which does not belong on a lamp.

M6.reason: In lineup.png, C is plainly the mod's model: a bare grey cube beside a bone, a checker test sphere and a ribcage. No player would take it for one of Half-Life's props, and nothing about it suggests a lamp.

M7.reason: A cube has no front, so the model gives no way to tell which side faces out or that a back sits against a wall. The pictures cannot confirm that it is mounted on its origin the way a wall fixture should be.

M8.reason: Measured: checkErrors is empty and the model has 12 triangles, well under twice the median of 62. The pictures show a closed box, not inside out and not floating.
